mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) over the past 6 months predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to increased corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows below 2% in the next quarter, 20d returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in FEDFUNDS above 2.0% triggers negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns due to increased discount rates eroding equity valuations.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS stays above 2.0% for >3 months without negative returns, reject (p>0.05 t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS (monetary tightening) and decline in UNRATE (lower labor costs) creates dual pressure that compresses inflation expectations, generating positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the interaction effect is not statistically significant (Rank IC <0.05) over 60 days, reject.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in UNRATE above 6.0% in the next month signals tight labor markets, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE stays above 6.0% for >2 months without positive returns, reject (p>0.05 t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in the INDPRO supply index above 100.1 in the next month indicates robust production capacity, spurring corporate investment and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO remains above 100.1% without positive returns, reject (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained FEDFUNDS rate above 4.0% for 3 months during a monetary tightening cycle triggers positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate policy adjustments and adjust portfolios.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS stays above 4.0% without positive returns, or if the tightening cycle ends without positive returns, reject (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the interaction effect is not statistically significant (Rank IC <0.05) over 60 days, reject.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 146,000 in the next month signals strong labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS stays above 146,000 without positive returns, reject (p>0.05 t-test).
